body: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.
summaryZh: 具身空间任务中的自进化智能体在面对多步骤、部分视觉证据的失败时，很难自动归因错误。本文提出了 HiMeco，一个受海马体记忆巩固和元认知监控启发的自进化智能体。通过海马-元认知反射机制诊断感知-探索-规划（PEP）中的失败，并将交互程序抽象为参数化技能。在保持模型参数冻结的前提下，HiMeco 在 ESI-Bench 上取得了最先进的性能，并在 EmbSpatial-Bench 上显著提升了准确率。
